$scope: The 4 `icons/resource-*` assets visible in review/compare/compare-icons.png (aether, cloudstone, provisions, skysteel), scored beside their counterparts. A SAMPLE, not the whole icons set — stated so the counts are not read as out of 16. NOTE the qwen-image-2512-positive column is a DIFFERENT PROMPT DIALECT — see COMPARISON.md's positive-dialect section — scored on the same four assets and the same taxonomy, which is what makes it readable, but it is not a controlled comparison with the other columns and must not be read as one. The gpt-image-2 column IS controlled: same four assets, same literal dialect, byte-identical prompts, only the model differs.

$notes.the shape of the error: Qwen read every one as a mobile-game ITEM CARD — decorative frame, bevelled centre panel, lighter background — rather than as a flat icon on the ash ground. The subject is right every time (aether droplet, cloudstone, wheat sheaf, skysteel ingot); it is the artefact type that is wrong, which is why criterion 1's arithmetic largely passes it and the eye does not.
$notes.gpt-image-2: The one artefact is `resource-provisions`, which carries a soft dark-green DROP SHADOW offset down and right of every stroke, against a brief that says 'no drop shadows' twice. It is invisible on the contact sheet and obvious at 3x: measured, its subject pixels occupy six lightness bands where the other three gpt icons occupy two or three. Nothing else in the sample is framed, bevelled, gradient-shaded or textured. The subject is right in all four and closer to the written plan than the reference is in two of them: cloudstone was asked for 'a single facet line across its face' and gpt draws one where FLUX draws an isometric cube with three, and skysteel was asked for 'one metal ingot seen slightly from above' drawn 'flat fills only' and gpt draws it flat. What gpt gets wrong is composition rather than rendering: `resource-aether` was asked for a teardrop with two short flame tips floating above a ring 'not touching it', and gpt returns a single flame — no separate tips — whose base overlaps the ring. That is a clause breach, not an artefact, so it is not scored here; it is in COMPARISON.md's icons verdict where it belongs.
$notes.the flux-2-pro non-flat figure is wrong: Scoring the gpt column meant looking at the reference column again, and `resource-skysteel` is an unambiguous 3D isometric ingot: bevelled edges, gradient-shaded faces, a specular edge highlight, and a silhouette lit from above — against a brief whose first paragraph says 'no gradients ... no bevels ... no 3D'. Measured the same way as the gpt note above, its subject spans six lightness bands from 8 to 14 while the other three FLUX icons span two or three. The honest figure for `non-flat rendering` in the flux-2-pro column is 1, not 0. It has NOT been edited, and that is not politeness: this column is mirrored into $pilot below, $pilot is summed across three repositories by claims.py, and the sum is transcribed into micro-brand/COMPARISON.md section 9.3. Changing it here alone turns claims.py red in two repositories and makes a third repository's published table wrong. It is the same rule that keeps promote.py out of shared.perRepository for now: a figure shared by three registries is corrected in one change across all three, or not at all. Recorded here as OWED so that the next person to touch section 9.3 corrects it in the same commit. Also corrected in $scope while looking: the sample was described as 'not out of 25' and the icons set has 16 members in both PLAN.json and MANIFEST.json.
$notes.why gpt-image-2 is not in $pilot: The pilot is a PROMPT-DIALECT experiment — the same assets asked for twice in two dialects — and gpt-image-2 is registered as `literal`, replaying the reference prompts byte for byte. Adding it to $pilot would put a second model in a block whose whole point is that only the wording changed, and would silently move an estate-wide total that three repositories transcribe.
$notes.both columns are scored AFTER normalise_: Neither endpoint delivers #12100f; the reference set only passes verify.py's flat-ground rule because normalise_ground.py was run over it, and the candidate only passes because it was run over that too. So a zero in that row means 'the delivered ground was FLAT enough to normalise', not 'the model hit the hex'. As delivered, gpt-image-2's grounds took FIVE distinct values over all 89 entries that carry the column and ranged #040404 to #140c0c, 63 of them at #0c0c0c — a bias rather than a spread, always too dark. The reference cannot be quoted against that on equal terms and the reason is recorded rather than papered over: `deliveredGround` is write-once and was added to this repository AFTER most of the reference run, so it exists for SIX of FLUX's 96 generations, at #141414, #1c1c1c, #242424, #2c2c2c, #2c242c and #342c3c — always too light. Six against 89 is not a comparison, and the #232324-to-#3f3a3b range in normalise_ground.py's own header is micro-brand's measurement carried into this file with the script, not this set's. Both models miss the hex, in opposite directions, and both score 0 on the row because the row asks whether the field is FLAT.
$notes.qwen-image-2512-positive: 4 of 4 framed and 4 of 4 bevelled, against a brief carrying no prohibition words at all. The item-card reading survived the rewrite intact: decorative border, bevelled centre panel, lighter inner field. It got WORSE in two places the literal set had right — resource-aether returned a large blue arc instead of a teardrop above a ring, and resource-skysteel returned a plain cube instead of a notched ingot, so 'idea not recognisable' goes from 0 of 4 to 2 of 4. The one clause that moved is the one about the field behind the subject: aether and skysteel came back on a mottled brown texture, which is worse than the literal set's flat dark panels.

$pilot.$scope: This repository's contribution to the estate-wide 15-asset positive-dialect pilot, micro-brand/COMPARISON.md section 9.3. These are the same 4 `icons/resource-*` assets the columns above score, restated under the row names that section's table uses, so the three repositories' contributions can be summed without a name-matching step. The other 11 are micro-brand's 2 currency marks and emberkin's 9 `types` icons. claims.py sums the three $pilot blocks, checks each one against the columns it was taken from via $columnAlias, and checks the section 9.3 table against the sum.

$columnAlias.non-flat (3D, bevel, gradient, glow): non-flat rendering (3D, bevel, gradient, glow, texture)
$columnAlias.ground not the flat ash field: ground not the flat ash field
$columnAlias.idea not recognisable from the plan: idea not recognisable from the plan

$unscored.construction guides drawn: Not scored over the icons sheet by this reviewer, so there is no figure to sum and claims.py does not pin that row of the section 9.3 table.
$unscored.recognisable pastiche of an existing art: Not scored here either. The absence is recorded rather than filled with a zero: an unscored row and a row scored zero are different statements, and only one of them is evidence.
